permanent_fix_required: Thread proposal_id from `aria-kernel cycle run` CLI through `run_enterprise_cycle` into the `pr_lifecycle` phase. Concrete steps: (1) add `--proposal-id` argument to the cycle CLI parser in cli.py adjacent to the existing `--plan-id` flag; (2) extend `run_enterprise_cycle(...)` signature with `proposal_id: str | None = None` kwarg and forward it to the pr_lifecycle phase callable; (3) inside the pr_lifecycle phase, when the phase is dispatched and `proposal_id` is None, raise `GovernanceError('pr_lifecycle phase requires --proposal-id; refusing to emit placeholder governance event')` instead of writing the current placeholder governance event; (4) when `proposal_id` is provided, dispatch to `pr_manager.open_pr_for_action(proposal_id=...)` so the phase produces a real PR action; (5) remove the placeholder governance write entirely; (6) remove this aria-debt marker from cycle.py:50-60 and add a regression test in `aria-kernel/tests/test_cycle_pr_lifecycle_proposal_id.py` covering the absent-proposal-id rejection and the present-proposal-id dispatch.
root_cause_summary: The cycle.py `run_enterprise_cycle` entry point does not accept a proposal_id parameter, so the pr_lifecycle phase cannot dispatch to pr_manager.open_pr_for_action which requires a proposal_id. The phase therefore emits a placeholder governance event instead of triggering a real PR action. The architectural fix is to thread proposal_id through the cycle entry point (CLI flag -> run_enterprise_cycle kwarg -> pr_lifecycle phase invocation) and fail closed when absent rather than emit a placeholder. The placeholder is itself architecturally honest (it does not pretend to act), but it accumulates audit-cost over time: every cycle run that opts into pr_lifecycle writes a no-op governance event; the audit trail records work that did not happen.

short_term_action_taken.rationale: Per CONTRACTS.md §6.6 + IDENTITY.md §3.6 Rule 3, every short-term workaround that does not permanently fix the underlying issue requires a tracked DEBT record with owner + due_date + source-side marker. The `aria-debt:DEBT-2026-05-10-001` line in cycle.py:56-61 makes the debt visible to readers of the source. The placeholder governance write itself is unchanged in this short-term action (the permanent fix per `permanent_fix_required` removes it).
